review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

3:1.sourceText: Κἀγώ, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἠδυνήθην λαλῆσαι ὑμῖν ὡς πνευματικοῖς ἀλλ’ ὡς σαρκίνοις, ὡς νηπίοις ἐν Χριστῷ.
3:1.targetText: Brothers, I could not address you as spiritual, but as worldly—as infants in Christ.

groups.note: κἀγώ ("and I") is rendered I; BSB has no word for and here.

3:2.sourceText: γάλα ὑμᾶς ἐπότισα, οὐ βρῶμα· οὔπω γὰρ ἐδύνασθε. Ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἔτι νῦν δύνασθε,
3:2.targetText: I gave you milk, not solid food, for you were not yet ready for solid food. In fact, you are still not ready,

groups.note: ἐπότισα ("I gave to drink") is rendered I gave.
ἐδύνασθε ("you were able") is rendered you were ready.
Ἀλλά ("but, indeed") is rendered In fact.
ἔτι νῦν ("still now") is rendered still.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the complement of ready; the Greek leaves it understood.

3:3.sourceText: ἔτι γὰρ σαρκικοί ἐστε. ὅπου γὰρ ἐν ὑμῖν ζῆλος καὶ ἔρις, οὐχὶ σαρκικοί ἐστε καὶ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον περιπατεῖτε;
3:3.targetText: for you are still worldly. For since there is jealousy and dissension among you, are you not worldly? Are you not walking in the way of man?

groups.note: ὅπου ("where") here gives the ground and is rendered since.
οὐχί governs both questions; BSB repeats not.
κατά ("according to") is rendered in the way of.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a second question instead of rendering καί ("and").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an existence verb; the Greek clause has no verb.

3:4.sourceText: ὅταν γὰρ λέγῃ τις Ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου, ἕτερος δέ Ἐγὼ Ἀπολλῶ, οὐκ ἄνθρωποί ἐστε;
3:4.targetText: For when one of you says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” are you not mere men?

groups.note: εἰμι with the genitive ("I am of Paul") is rendered I follow; BSB repeats follow where the Greek leaves the verb understood.

unmappedSource.reason: μέν marks the first side of the contrast and has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds the group; the Greek has only τις ("someone").
English adds emphasis; the Greek has only ἄνθρωποι ("men").

3:5.sourceText: τί οὖν ἐστιν Ἀπολλῶς; τί δέ ἐστιν Παῦλος; διάκονοι δι’ ὧν ἐπιστεύσατε, καὶ ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκεν.
3:5.targetText: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? They are servants through whom you believed, as the Lord has assigned to each his role.

groups.note: ἔδωκεν ("gave") is rendered has assigned.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render this καί ("and").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula; the Greek has only the noun.
English supplies an object for assigned.

3:6.sourceText: ἐγὼ ἐφύτευσα, Ἀπολλῶς ἐπότισεν, ἀλλὰ ὁ Θεὸς ηὔξανεν·
3:6.targetText: I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.

groups.note: ηὔξανεν ("caused to grow") is rendered made … grow.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; the Greek verb has none.
English joins the clauses with and; the Greek has no connective.
English supplies an object; the Greek verb has none.
English supplies an object; the Greek verb has none.

3:7.sourceText: ὥστε οὔτε ὁ φυτεύων ἐστίν τι οὔτε ὁ ποτίζων, ἀλλ’ ὁ αὐξάνων Θεός.
3:7.targetText: So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but only God, who makes things grow.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds an adverb; the Greek has none.
English supplies an object; the Greek participle has none.

3:8.sourceText: ὁ φυτεύων δὲ καὶ ὁ ποτίζων ἕν εἰσιν, ἕκαστος δὲ τὸν ἴδιον μισθὸν λήμψεται κατὰ τὸν ἴδιον κόπον.
3:8.targetText: He who plants and he who waters are one in purpose, and each will be rewarded according to his own labor.

groups.note: μισθὸν λήμψεται ("will receive a reward") is rendered will be rewarded.

unmappedSource.reason: δέ continues the thought and has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render ἴδιον ("his own") with the reward; his own is given with labor.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds the respect in which they are one; the Greek has only ἕν ("one").

3:9.sourceText: Θεοῦ γάρ ἐσμεν συνεργοί· Θεοῦ γεώργιον, Θεοῦ οἰκοδομή ἐστε.
3:9.targetText: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, God’s building.

3:10.sourceText: Κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ὡς σοφὸς ἀρχιτέκτων θεμέλιον ἔθηκα, ἄλλος δὲ ἐποικοδομεῖ. ἕκαστος δὲ βλεπέτω πῶς ἐποικοδομεῖ.
3:10.targetText: By the grace God has given me, I laid a foundation as an expert builder, and someone else is building on it. But each one must be careful how he builds.

groups.note: τὴν δοθεῖσαν ("that was given") is rendered actively, with God as the giver.
βλεπέτω ("let him see to it") is rendered must be careful.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; the Greek verb has none.

3:11.sourceText: θεμέλιον γὰρ ἄλλον οὐδεὶς δύναται θεῖναι παρὰ τὸν κείμενον, ὅς ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός.
3:11.targetText: For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.

groups.note: τὸν κείμενον ("the one lying there") is rendered the one … laid.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds already; the Greek has only the participle.

3:12.sourceText: εἰ δέ τις ἐποικοδομεῖ ἐπὶ τὸν θεμέλιον χρυσίον, ἀργύριον, λίθους τιμίους, ξύλα, χόρτον, καλάμην,
3:12.targetText: If anyone builds on this foundation using gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,

groups.note: The article points back to the foundation just named.
BSB's Greek text has a different form of this word with the same meaning.

unmappedSource.reason: δέ continues the thought and has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a verb for the materials, which in Greek are the objects of builds.
English adds or before the last item; the Greek list has no connective.

3:13.sourceText: ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον φανερὸν γενήσεται· ἡ γὰρ ἡμέρα δηλώσει, ὅτι ἐν πυρὶ ἀποκαλύπτεται, καὶ ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον ὁποῖόν ἐστιν τὸ πῦρ αὐτὸ δοκιμάσει.
3:13.targetText: his workmanship will be evident, because the Day will bring it to light. It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will prove the quality of each man’s work.

groups.note: ἑκάστου ("of each one") is rendered his, referring to the builder.
γάρ ("for") is rendered because.
δηλώσει ("will make it clear") is rendered will bring … to light.
ὁποῖον ("of what sort") is rendered the quality.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence and does not render ὅτι ("because").

BSB turns the clause "what sort it is" into a noun phrase, so ἐστιν has no English word.
BSB does not render αὐτό ("itself").

3:14.sourceText: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον μενεῖ ὃ ἐποικοδόμησεν, μισθὸν λήμψεται·
3:14.targetText: If what he has built survives, he will receive a reward.

groups.note: τὸ ἔργον … ὅ ("the work that") is rendered what.
μενεῖ ("will remain") is rendered survives.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render τινος ("anyone's"); the he of has built comes from the verb.

3:15.sourceText: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον κατακαήσεται, ζημιωθήσεται, αὐτὸς δὲ σωθήσεται, οὕτως δὲ ὡς διὰ πυρός.
3:15.targetText: If it is burned up, he will suffer loss. He himself will be saved, but only as if through the flames.

groups.note: τὸ ἔργον ("the work") is rendered it.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render τινος ("anyone's").
BSB starts a new sentence without rendering δέ.
BSB does not render οὕτως ("in this way") separately.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds an adverb; the Greek has none.

3:16.sourceText: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ναὸς Θεοῦ ἐστε καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν οἰκεῖ;
3:16.targetText: Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple, and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?

groups.note: ὅτι governs both clauses; BSB repeats that.

3:17.sourceText: εἴ τις τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ φθείρει, φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ Θεός· ὁ γὰρ ναὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἅγιός ἐστιν, οἵτινές ἐστε ὑμεῖς.
3:17.targetText: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.

groups.note: The relative οἵτινες ("which") is rendered and … that temple, as BSB starts a new clause.

3:18.sourceText: Μηδεὶς ἑαυτὸν ἐξαπατάτω· εἴ τις δοκεῖ σοφὸς εἶναι ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ, μωρὸς γενέσθω, ἵνα γένηται σοφός,
3:18.targetText: Let no one deceive himself. If any of you thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool, so that he may become wise.

groups.note: The infinitive εἶναι ("to be") is rendered he is, with the thinker as its subject.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:19.sourceText: ἡ γὰρ σοφία τοῦ κόσμου τούτου μωρία παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ ἐστιν. γέγραπται γάρ Ὁ δρασσόμενος τοὺς σοφοὺς ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτῶν·
3:19.targetText: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God’s sight. As it is written: “He catches the wise in their craftiness.”

groups.note: παρά ("before, in the judgment of") is rendered in … sight.
γάρ ("for") is rendered As.

3:20.sourceText: καὶ πάλιν Κύριος γινώσκει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς τῶν σοφῶν, ὅτι εἰσὶν μάταιοι.
3:20.targetText: And again, “The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile.”

3:21.sourceText: ὥστε μηδεὶς καυχάσθω ἐν ἀνθρώποις· πάντα γὰρ ὑμῶν ἐστιν,
3:21.targetText: Therefore, stop boasting in men. All things are yours,

groups.note: μηδείς ("no one") with the imperative is rendered as the command stop.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render γάρ ("for") here.

3:22.sourceText: εἴτε Παῦλος εἴτε Ἀπολλῶς εἴτε Κηφᾶς, εἴτε κόσμος εἴτε ζωὴ εἴτε θάνατος, εἴτε ἐνεστῶτα εἴτε μέλλοντα, πάντα ὑμῶν,
3:22.targetText: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or the present or the future. All of them belong to you,

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek has only the genitive ὑμῶν (as Galatians 3:29).

3:23.sourceText: ὑμεῖς δὲ Χριστοῦ, Χριστὸς δὲ Θεοῦ.
3:23.targetText: and you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
